Meta Pixel with Cookie Compliance

Cookbook · guide · Last verified 25 November 2026 · View raw markdown (for agents)

In short: keep the Cookie Compliance snippet as the first script in <head>, then paste the Meta Pixel below it. The banner holds the recognised Facebook loader until the visitor allows Ad Personalisation, in regions whose rule requires consent first.

You need #

  • The Cookie Compliance snippet already installed as the first script in <head> (see plain-html or your platform guide).
  • Your Meta Pixel ID and the Pixel code from Meta Events Manager.
  • Edit access to the same template, theme or head field as the banner snippet.

Where it goes #

Meta's docs place the Pixel between the <head> tags. With Cookie Compliance installed, keep the banner snippet first, then paste the Pixel below it. The code shape loads fbevents.js and includes a <noscript> image fallback:

<!-- Cookie Compliance snippet first, then Meta's Pixel block: -->
<script>
  !function(f,b,e,v,n,t,s){/* Meta's loader */}(window,document,'script',
  'https://connect.facebook.net/en_US/fbevents.js');
  fbq('init', 'YOUR-PIXEL-ID');
  fbq('track', 'PageView');
</script>
<noscript><img height="1" width="1" style="display:none"
  src="https://www.facebook.com/tr?id=YOUR-PIXEL-ID&ev=PageView&noscript=1"/></noscript>

What the order controls #

The banner recognises connect.facebook.net (fbevents.js) and holds it under category 4 Ad Personalisation by default. The whole inline block is held when it names that address. In regions whose rule requires consent first, the Pixel waits until the visitor allows that category; it starts after Allow. A script placed above the banner snippet runs straight away.

Confirm the result #

View the page source: the banner snippet comes first in <head>, the Pixel after it. Before choosing, in a region whose rule requires consent first, _fbp (and _fbc once available) are absent; the held script shows type="javascript/blocked" in the Elements panel. After Allow, those cookies appear. Browser checks: plain-html; full procedure: verify-install.

Gotchas #

  • Meta Consent Mode on (Professional plan). The connect.facebook.net loader then loads straight away with a denied signal until the visitor chooses. Judge by the cookies (_fbp, _fbc), not by whether the loader request appears. See Meta Pixel cookie consent.
  • A script above the banner snippet runs straight away. Keep the Pixel below the Cookie Compliance snippet.
